# Mini RISC-V SoC

A small, synthesizable RISC-V system-on-chip in SystemVerilog, checked instruction by instruction against
the Spike reference model, and taken through physical implementation on the open sky130 process.

- **Core:** 5-stage pipelined RV32I (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with full forwarding, a one-cycle load-use
  stall, branches resolved in EX, Zicsr, Zifencei, and precise M-mode traps and interrupts at a
  single commit point.
- **Memory system:** 2 KB direct-mapped I-cache and D-cache (write-through, 2-entry write buffer),
  an arbiter, an AXI4-Lite master and interconnect, and an AXI4-Lite-to-APB bridge.
- **Peripherals:** CLINT (timer, software interrupt), PLIC (2 sources), UART (8N1, FIFOs) and an SPI
  master (modes 0-3).
- **Verification:**
  - directed tests and the official riscv-tests;
  - instruction-by-instruction co-simulation against Spike, both offline and in lockstep over DPI;
  - riscv-dv random programs;
  - a UVM environment with a register model;
  - functional coverage;
  - mutation checks that prove each regression catches the bugs it is meant to catch.
- **Physical design:** LibreLane on sky130A, with the caches' arrays in sky130 SRAM macros.

Every figure below is regenerated from a real simulation or implementation run by `make figures`,
and every number in this README is read from a result file in `build/results/` (`scripts/make_readme.py`).

![Block diagram](docs/figures/block_diagram.png)

**Block diagram.** The SoC as instantiated in rtl/soc_top.sv and rtl/periph_subsys.sv: core, caches, arbiter, AXI4-Lite master and interconnect, external memory port, APB bridge and the four peripherals.<br>

## The pipeline at work

![Pipeline hazards](docs/figures/pipeline_hazards.png)

**Pipeline hazards.** A load followed at once by a use of its result: the hazard unit holds IF/ID for one cycle and inserts a bubble into EX; the dependent instruction then takes the loaded value from MEM/WB (fwd_rs1/fwd_rs2).<br>
<sub>test: hz_load_use (sw/tests/hz_load_use.S); configuration: core model, ideal memory; data: `waveform build/waves/figures/pipeline_hazards.fst`; command: `make wave TEST=build/directed/hz_load_use`</sub>

![D-cache refill](docs/figures/dcache_refill.png)

**D-cache refill.** A load misses in the D-cache: the cache reads the 16-byte line as four single-beat AXI4-Lite reads on the external memory port (one transaction at a time through the arbiter, master and interconnect), then answers the core, which is stalled meanwhile. The I-cache is idle: the loop runs from it.<br>
<sub>test: cache_dside (sw/tests/cache_dside.S); configuration: SoC model, ideal memory; data: `waveform build/waves/figures/dcache_refill.fst`; command: `make wave TEST=build/directed/cache_dside WAVE_SIM=soc`</sub>

![Timer interrupt](docs/figures/timer_interrupt.png)

**Timer interrupt.** mtime reaches mtimecmp and the CLINT raises MTIP; the core takes the interrupt at the commit point (end of MEM) after the instruction there: mepc becomes the next pc, MIE is cleared, the younger instructions are flushed (bubbles) and fetch is redirected to the handler (mtvec, 0x8000005c). Its line misses in the I-cache and is refilled over the bus, so the handler's first instruction reaches ID 39 cycles after the interrupt is taken.<br>
<sub>test: timer_irq (sw/tests/timer_irq.c); configuration: SoC model, ideal memory; data: `waveform build/waves/figures/timer_interrupt.fst`; command: `make wave TEST=build/ctests/timer_irq WAVE_SIM=soc`</sub>

## Peripherals

![UART loopback](docs/figures/uart_loopback.png)

**UART loopback.** The first byte the program sends ('H', 0x48): start bit, eight data bits LSB first, stop bit, 8 clock cycles per bit; the receiver (TX wired to RX in the testbench) samples each bit in its middle and pushes the byte into the RX FIFO.<br>
<sub>test: uart_loopback (sw/tests/uart_loopback.c); configuration: SoC model, ideal memory; data: `waveform build/waves/figures/uart_loopback.fst`; command: `make wave TEST=build/ctests/uart_loopback WAVE_SIM=soc`</sub>

![SPI modes 0-3](docs/figures/spi_modes.png)

**SPI modes 0-3.** The first frame in each SPI mode, one panel each: SCLK idles at CPOL; with CPHA = 0 the first bit is on MOSI before the first edge and both sides sample on leading edges, with CPHA = 1 data changes on leading edges and is sampled on trailing ones. The bytes are decoded from the waveform at the sampling edges; MISO comes from the testbench's SPI slave model.<br>
<sub>test: spi_modes (sw/tests/spi_modes.c); configuration: SoC model, ideal memory; data: `waveform build/waves/figures/spi_modes.fst`; command: `make wave TEST=build/ctests/spi_modes WAVE_SIM=soc`</sub>

## Verification evidence

The core is checked against the Spike reference model instruction by instruction:
- **Offline:** the retirement traces are compared after the run.
- **Lockstep:** Spike runs inside the simulation over DPI. Every interrupt the core takes is injected
  into Spike, and every MMIO load is answered with the value the core received. This is what lets
  programs with interrupts and devices be compared.

![Regression dashboard](docs/figures/regression_dashboard.png)

**Regression dashboard.** Passed and total runs of every regression, each test in each memory configuration and seed, read from the result files of the make targets; and the size of the lockstep comparison against Spike.<br>
<sub>test: every suite; seed: 101 202 303; configuration: ideal, random latency, random interrupts; data: `build/results/*.json`; command: `make accept-phase7 (and the earlier accept-phaseN)`</sub>

![Functional coverage](docs/figures/functional_coverage.png)

**Functional coverage.** Hit count of every SVA cover point (forwarding paths, load-use, branch after load, CSR sequences, interrupts during a stall or flush, every exception and interrupt cause, cache corner cases) merged over the regression.<br>
<sub>test: the Phase 2 suite on the core and cache models, every SoC and C test; seed: 101 202 303; configuration: ideal, ideal+irq, random+irq; data: `build/results/coverage.json`; command: `make coverage`</sub>

![UVM coverage](docs/figures/uvm_coverage.png)

**UVM coverage.** Coverage bins of the UVM environment for the bus and peripheral subsystem: AXI4-Lite direction x region x response x strobes x AW/W order, UART bit lengths and data, SPI mode x bit order.<br>
<sub>test: reg_reset, reg_bitbash, uart_tx, uart_rx, spi, irq, axil_order; seed: 101 202 303; configuration: random latency on the memory port; data: `build/results/uvm.json`; command: `make uvm`</sub>

![Mutation checks](docs/figures/mutation_checks.png)

**Mutation checks.** Bugs deliberately injected into the RTL, one at a time, and the regression that has to catch each one (scripts/cosim_mutants.py; the co-simulation mutants must also pass the self-checking tests, so only co-simulation can catch them). rtl/ is restored and checksummed after every mutant.<br>
<sub>test: per plan; seed: 101 202 303; configuration: per plan; data: `build/results/mutants_*.json`; command: `make cosim-mutants cache-mutants bus-mutants periph-mutants lockstep-mutants uvm-mutants`</sub>

## Reproducing

```sh
make check-tools PHASE=8   # toolchain report, with install hints
make submodules            # riscv-tests, uvm-core, riscv-isa-sim (Spike), riscv-dv
make test                  # lint, every regression, co-simulation, lockstep, UVM, coverage
make accept-phase7         # UVM, lockstep, riscv-dv, coverage, mutation checks
make accept-phase8         # sky130 implementation (LibreLane in Docker)
make results               # every regression and mutation plan whose result files the README reads
make figures               # every figure in this README, and the README itself
make wave TEST=build/directed/hz_load_use FROM=100 TO=200   # a waveform for Surfer
```

Seeds 101, 202 and 303 are used throughout. Any single run can be repeated with
`make riscv-tests MEM=random SEED=202` and similar targets.
